$comment: SEC-01 baseline. Every entry here is a credential that IS ALREADY IN GIT
HISTORY and cannot be removed without rewriting it. The allowlist exists so
that the history secret scan fails on anything NEW while the known set is
pending the coordinated purge -- it is not an acceptance of these values.
Entries are keyed by sha256[:16] of the credential value. The value itself
appears nowhere in this repository, this file, or any CI log; the digest
identifies it for rotation tracking without disclosing it.
DELETE THIS FILE'S known_exposures ARRAY IMMEDIATELY AFTER
scripts/security/purge_history_secrets.sh RUNS. An empty array is the
post-purge steady state: the history scan then blocks on every finding.
Removal is verified by `scan_secrets.py --mode history`, which must report
Allowlisting a NEW value is a security decision, not a build fix. Only add
an entry for a confirmed false positive, and only with a named reviewer.

known_exposures.reason: SEC-01 P0, credential side CLOSED. The repository owner confirmed on 2026-08-14 that all three historical provider keys were deleted at their providers and that only newly generated keys are in use. This digest therefore identifies a value that no longer authenticates. Independently corroborated to the extent the repository can: scan_secrets.py --mode worktree and --mode range 0615921..HEAD both report 0 findings, so none of the replacement keys has entered the tree or any commit on this branch. The value remains in history until the coordinated purge, which is now hygiene rather than exposure.

ACCEPTED RISK -- repository owner, 2026-08-14. Not rotated, by decision. Rationale as given: these are auto-generated values scoped to the local Docker stack, reused nowhere else, so disclosure grants nothing an attacker could reach. Independently corroborated: compose binds every one of these services to 127.0.0.1 (SQL Server 14330, Neo4j 7474/7687, MongoDB 27017, Valkey 6379, Temporal 7233, Vault 8200), so none is reachable off-host as configured. Revisit if the stack is ever bound to a routable interface, shared between hosts, or promoted to an environment carrying real data.
